title: Typed Cache Tensors Design Review
eyebrow: Review of the codex design for issue #4525 (positron-ai/tron)
h1: Does the codex design for typed KV-cache tensors hold up?
meta: Reviewed 2026-09-22 UTC by Claude (Fable 5.1) for jhan. Design reviewed: [status/design-new-tensor-type.html](design-new-tensor-type.html) (67,216 bytes, finalized 2026-09-22 00:22 UTC). Sources pinned to main f46e48ba (the design's snapshot), main 98bb8cb2 (the live tip when the design was written) and PR 4424 head 30c4ac82cb. Main moved to 2880c3aa9b at 01:14 UTC on 2026-09-22, during this review; none of the design's step-list source files changed in those five commits.
short_version: Issue #4525 captures what jhan and Ben asked for. Two additions would make its body self-contained: one sentence naming the problem (bare bf16 pointers carry no layout), and one-line definitions of pair-interleaved V, native K and PR 4424's blocked K.

jhan's reading of Ben's reservation is right: the address formula belongs in the view, and storage stays a separate owner. The design should say so plainly instead of "mostly right", and should list its three departures from Ben as questions for him.

The design is sound on layouts, ownership and kernel typing, and it can go to an implementing agent after nine major edits: name the function chain of the model's V save, correct the revision table (98bb8cb2 is the live main, not a stale copy), add an accessor mapping table, defer slices and iteration, state the 8-lane build rule, spell out the arena construction form, and rewrite the required-CI paragraph.

words: tron
the inference program under test; its source is the positron-ai/tron repository
the open draft pull request "VNNI K: store the K cache of 128-dimension heads in the AMX VNNI layout, with a shared block save" (branch jhan-amx-vnniK, head 30c4ac82cb)
Ben
the tron maintainer who reviewed PR 4424 on 2026-09-21 (three comments: a worker-index question, a review asking for typed tensors, and an API sketch)
codex, the design
codex is the agent jhan asked to answer Ben; the design is the page it wrote, status/design-new-tensor-type.html
issue #4525
the GitHub issue codex created for the new work; jhan edited its title and first sentence on 2026-09-22 00:10 UTC
KV cache, K, V
the saved key (K) and value (V) vectors of earlier tokens; attention reads them
page, slot, head, D

a page holds 64 token positions; a slot is the cache region of one layer (or of several layers that share it); a head is one attention head; D is the head size, the number of values per token per head (128 for PR 4424's models)
bf16
the 16-bit brain floating-point format used for cached K and V
AMX, AVX-512, 8-lane build
AMX and AVX-512 are CPU instruction sets. tron's vector width TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 16 with AVX-512 and 8 without; the 8-lane build stores V row-major, so it has no pair-interleaved V
VNNI layout
a storage order the AMX tile multiply reads directly as its second operand. The design calls it "packed"
pair-interleaved V (the design's "packed V")
today's V storage in the 16-lane build: for each dimension, tokens 2p and 2p+1 sit next to each other. Element offset = (token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2
blocked VNNI K (the design's "blocked packed K")
PR 4424's K storage for 128-dimension heads: two consecutive dimensions of one token share a 4-byte unit, and 16 tokens share one 64-byte line
native K
today's K storage: one token's D values consecutive in memory (row-major)
expr, view, const_view, tensor

tron's expression interface (h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp), its typed pointer views over regularly laid-out memory and their read-only form (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp), and its owning arrays (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp)
kv_block
the struct that holds K then V for one head of one slot in one page (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp)
set_v, get_v, append_v, scaled_v, v_data
today's V functions in kv_cache.hpp: write one token, read one token, copy one token between pages, compute the weighted V sum, and return the raw pointer of a V plane
save_v_impl, save_k_impl
the model functions (h/tron/models/model.hpp) that store one token's V and K into the cache during a forward pass
Zero-Initialized V Slots invariant

the rule in kv_cache.hpp that every even-token V write zeroes its odd partner row. The weighted sum reads a whole pair even when the token count is odd, and NaN times 0 is NaN, so the padding row must be zero
GOF

group of four: four tokens of K and V data staged for the FPGA's hardware KV cache, as one 8 KB K block and one 8 KB V block (h/tron/gof.hpp header comment). The staging code reaches a page's rows through the page_info callbacks declared in that file. The design defines GOF differently; finding F24 corrects it
EAGLE
the speculative model; its cache uses an extra storage region
parent PR, child PR
the parent is the new PR that issue #4525 asks for; the child is PR 4424 after it is rebased onto the parent
main tip, snapshot

98bb8cb2 (2026-09-19) was the main tip when the design was written and when this review started; main moved to 2880c3aa9b at 01:14 UTC on 2026-09-22. The snapshot is commit f46e48ba (2026-09-15), the base GitHub records for PR 4424 and the revision the design reviewed
CI, Nix test build, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, TRON_K_VNNI
CI is the automated build and test. The Nix test build is the required CI lane. The two CMake options compile the AMX attention kernels and PR 4424's K layout; the Nix lane sets neither
finder, verifier

review agents. Eight finders each read the design through one lens; three verifiers then tried to refute every finding (a source-truth lens, a design-text-fairness lens, an intent lens). A finding survived only if at least two verifiers could not refute it
blocker, major, minor, note

issue_outro: **Verdict: the issue captures the request.** Every item Ben asked for and every item in jhan's plan appears in the body or follows from it. Two additions would make the body self-contained for a reader who has not opened the PR thread. First, one problem sentence before Scope: cache K and V planes are passed as bare bf16 pointers whose type does not record the layout, and PR 4424 adds a third layout. Second, one-line definitions of pair-interleaved V, native K, and PR 4424's blocked K. A third, optional clause on step 2 would restate jhan's goal: after the rebase, PR 4424's K layout is a local change inside the new tensor type, not a change in model and attention code.

Two smaller points. Ben's straw-man states three constraints the scope bullets carry only in generic words (construct the storage in the arena rather than cast; no raw pointer relabelled as packed; no clearing added to allocation); the design covers all three, so this is a gap in the public record only (F20). The issue names Ben twice; jhan's standing rule for issues drafted for him is roles and links only, and the 00:11 UTC edit under jhan's login left the names in, so this is jhan's call (F21). The design page and its saved evidence files still carry the pre-edit title "before PR #4424" and the paragraph jhan deleted (F50).
ben_intro: Ben's sketch has three parts: a layout struct with a static offset function, a storage owner templated on the layout, and a view templated on the layout. His reservation was: "I'm not entirely convinced of the necessity of separate k_vnni_layout from vnni_view but regardless, it's a starting point". jhan read this as: the layout should be the view, and agreed. The design agrees too and says jhan's interpretation is "mostly right".
ben_outro: **jhan's reading is right on the point Ben raised.** Ben's doubt concerns only the separate layout type. Folding the offset formula into the view removes that type. Storage stays a separate owner in Ben's sketch, in jhan's reading, and in the design.
Two precisions the design should state instead of "mostly right":
ben_bullets: Ben's sketch is not a chain layout -> storage -> view. The layout type is a template parameter of both the storage and the view (vnni_tensor<Layout> and vnni_view<T, Layout>), and the view calls Layout::offset. jhan's chain wording describes the dependency, not the shape. Nothing in jhan's reading proposed merging storage into the view, so the design's storage sentence does not correct a mistake (F03).

Ben voiced a doubt, not a decision. The design turns it into a rule ("Simplify: each view type contains its address calculation") without saying that the merge is the design's own choice and that Ben should confirm it. The design does fix the resulting type shape (vnni_tensor<R, D>, vnni_view<T, R, D>, no Layout parameter), so an implementer is not left guessing; the verifiers rejected that concern (F06 in section 7). The trade-off is still worth one sentence for Ben: one view type per layout (a V view now, a K view in the child) repeats the const conversion, the deleted rvalue access and the friend accessor, instead of one template over a layout parameter.

The design departs from Ben in three further places and lists no questions for him (F02, F04). It makes a const view yield read-only rows where Ben wrote "as with std::span, a const view object does not make its elements const"; the design flags this and cites the rank-2 view, but the repository is split (the rank-1 view states Ben's rule verbatim in a comment), and the design never says what a const row yields. It replaces Ben's at(token, dim) with operator[][] without saying why (the expr base requires operator[]). It adds slices, iterators and generic expression assignment that Ben did not ask for (F08). jhan's item 3 said to stop and write questions when disagreeing with Ben. Stopping was not required, because the reservation was soft and the merge is the direction jhan and Ben both lean to. A short "Questions for Ben" block in the design, and a one-paragraph reply in the PR thread pointing him at issue #4525, would close the loop. As of 2026-09-22 00:3x UTC the PR thread has no reply after Ben's sketch and the issue has no cross-reference from the PR.
findings_intro: Eight finders produced 80 raw candidates, grouped into 59 distinct findings. Each was put to three verifiers who tried to refute it; 49 survived and the 10 that did not are listed in section 7. A completeness critic then added 9 candidates, and all 9 survived the same verification, for 58 findings in total. Severities below are the lead's final grades; where they differ from the finder's grade, the finding says so under Lead's reading.
partner_intro: The most consequential finding (F01) turns on the Zero-Initialized V Slots invariant. The figure shows one V pair on a page offset that is being reused, under today's code and under the two write operations the design defines. Only the third lane is safe, and the design never says by name that the model's save path takes it.
strengths: Section 6 names the trickiest behavior first: the odd padding row must be zero because NaN times zero is NaN, and the model's write order must not change; this matches Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] and scaled_v's pair round-up exactly.

Section 6 states the arena construction constraints that Ben demanded (construct the storage type, no cast of the SIMD array, no clearing on allocation or restore, trivial default construction) and adds the C++ reason (accessors reinterpret_cast uninitialized bytes, so a constructor never runs by itself).

Section 5 keeps Ben's access rules (no public pointer constructor, no data(), friend accessor in detail::vnni_access, deleted rvalue as_view, mutable-to-const conversion only) and keeps native K on the existing view so dotter is untouched; the K-side change is limited to a kernel parameter type.

Section 4 gives the three layout formulas with a checked script and the correct observation that blocked K is not a coordinate swap of packed V; the formulas match kv_block's index comment and k_vnni::index at the child head.

Section 3 draws the right boundary for the split: TRON_K_VNNI, the packed-K kernels, helper-thread state and generated helper calls stay in the child, and the design warns against copying whole files from the child branch because main moved.

Section 6 (Copy, append, hardware preparation) preserves the whole-plane byte copy, all four even/odd append combinations, and the caller-owned GOF scratch, and keeps the child's K callback signature change in the child.

Section 8 lists the three build configurations (16-lane, 16-lane with AMX, 8-lane) and states plainly that the Nix CI build leaves AMX off and that a disabled-feature placeholder success proves nothing; it also declares that nothing was compiled or run.
Section 7 tells the agent to search all callers before removing accessors and forbids replacing the vector V operations with scalar loops, which protects the hot path.

rejected_intro: These candidates were raised by a finder and refuted by at least two of the three verifiers. They are listed so that a reader who has the same doubt can see why it did not hold.
method: The lead first verified the ground facts by hand: the live issue and its edit history, Ben's three comments from the GitHub API, the commit graph (f46e48ba is an ancestor of the live tip 98bb8cb2), the files that changed between them, and the tron source lines the design cites. Those facts were written to a file every agent read first [evidence/claude-review/lead-verified-facts.md].

The design was then reviewed by a workflow of agents. Every finding on this page carries the evidence its finder cited and the votes of its three verifiers. The lead read every surviving finding and its votes before publishing, and corrected wording where a verifier's correction was right.

Counts: 8 finders, 80 raw candidates, 59 groups, 177 verification votes, 49 confirmed and 10 rejected; the critic added 9 candidates and all 9 survived their 27 votes. 214 agents in total. The lead re-graded 12 findings to the verifiers' majority severity (F01 blocker to major; F03, F13, F14, F15, F17 major to minor; C03, F20, F28, F31, F43 minor to note; C08 note to minor) and amended five claims where facts changed during the review (main moved twice) or where a verifier corrected a number (94 characters, not 267; 14 links, not 15). One rejected candidate (F36) came from an incomplete summary of Ben's sketch in the lead's own facts file; verification against the primary source caught it.
method_bullets: Finder lenses: issue capture; fidelity to Ben and to jhan's reading; C++ interface soundness against tron's expr, view, slice and tensor machinery; behavior preservation (zero-init invariant, conversions, copies, staging); PR split and process (revisions, CI, repository rules); simplicity and scope; handoff actionability (can an agent implement it without guessing; citation spot-check); formulas and page quality.

Verifier lenses: source truth (re-derive from tron source, Ben's text, the issue), design-text fairness (does the design already handle it elsewhere), intent (does the finding respect what Ben and jhan asked for; assign consequence-based severity).

Not done: no C++ was compiled, no test was built or run, no benchmark was taken. The design itself states the same limits. Claims about compile-time behavior (triviality, aliases, concept checks) rest on reading the headers at the pinned commits.

Files: the facts the lead verified first [lead-verified-facts.md](../evidence/claude-review/lead-verified-facts.md); raw candidates [raw-findings-round1.json](../evidence/claude-review/raw-findings-round1.json); workflow result with every vote [workflow-result.json](../evidence/claude-review/workflow-result.json); the lead's re-grades and amendments [overrides.json](../evidence/claude-review/overrides.json); page data [findings.json](../evidence/claude-review/findings.json); generator [gen_review.py](../evidence/claude-review/gen_review.py); all votes rendered [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-votes.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-votes.html).

confirmed.title: Model V save path: the design never names which operation save_v_impl calls
confirmed.section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve (V padding and write ordering) and 7. Implementation steps, step 5 (Model saves)
confirmed.claim: Ambiguity: the design never says which of its two V write operations save_v_impl (the model.hpp function that stores one token's V vector into the cache) calls after the parent PR. Today save_v_impl calls page::set_v. The even-token path of set_v zero-extends each value, so the odd partner row becomes zero. That zeroing is the only thing that keeps the padding row zero when a page offset is reused, because clear_kv_complete_at (the function run when an offset is reassigned) resets completion counters and never touches V bytes. Two design sentences point the model path at the new 'logical operations', and the design defines the logical row operation row.set() as pair-preserving. An implementer who follows those sentences leaves a stale odd row in place after an even write on a reused offset. scaled_v (the weighted V sum) rounds its loop bound up to a full pair, so a stale NaN in that odd row is multiplied by weight 0 and the sum becomes NaN. The existing regression test calls page::set_v directly, so it would keep passing while the model path regressed.
confirmed.evidence: h/tron/models/model.hpp:2818-2819@f46e48bab498: `pg.template set_v<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, j, &vs[ix][kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size]);` is the 16-lane model write. h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2301@f46e48bab498: `bf16x32 even = _mm512_cvtepu16_epi32(lo);` (zero-extend, odd partner becomes 0). kv_cache.hpp:2062-2064: Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] "Invariant: every even-indexed V write zeroes the odd partner. ... set_v: even paths zero-extend via cvtepu16_epi32." kv_cache.hpp:2078: `const size_t end = (count + 1) / 2 * 2;`. kv_cache.hpp:1791-1795: clear_kv_complete_at stores 0 into kv_saves_ counters only. h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:750-757@f46e48bab498: comment "so a prior use of this page's offsets (before eviction) doesn't leak" (offsets are reused with old V bytes). t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2449-2472@f46e48bab498: SECTION "single-token dirty-buffer reuse" poisons slot 1 then calls `p->set_v(..., 0, v.data.data())` directly.
confirmed.design_quote: "Keep existing page methods where needed. Make them call the new logical operations." / "Call typed K/V operations using logical coordinates. Remove V layout choices from save_v_impl, which saves model values in the cache." / "// Logical public operations remain ordinary assignment and conversion. destination_view[token].set(source_expr);" / "The cache chooses when to use the behavior for a newly added row."
confirmed.recommendation: Add to section 6 and to step 5, in these words: "save_v_impl writes every token through the cache-append operation (append_v_row: on an even token it writes the even row and zeroes the odd row in one store; on an odd token it preserves the even row). It never calls row.set(). page::set_v keeps its name and its zeroing behavior and is the only caller of append_v_row for model saves. In the parent PR no production code calls ordinary assignment on a packed V row." Add a verification row: poison an odd row, write the even partner through the same page method that save_v_impl calls (not a test-only path), then check scaled_v with count = 1 produces no NaN.

votes.reason:

Short version: the descriptive part of F28 is accurate, but the design's prose already carries the whole pair-zeroing invariant, so the missing figure has no consequence for the implementing agent or for Ben. Under the intent lens this is a presentation preference, not a design defect.

Evidence I checked:

- The three diagrams are CSS label boxes with text arrows, and the page has no <svg> element [design-new-tensor-type.html:79-88, 93-101, 274-283; grep for "<svg" returns nothing]. That part of F28 holds.
- Diagram 1 (owner -> view -> kernel) repeats the bullet list directly above it [html:75-77 vs 79-88]. Diagram 2 (main -> parent -> child) repeats the revision table and the section prose [html:93-101 vs 102-110]. That part holds too.
- The pair-zeroing invariant in tron: Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] says "every even-indexed V write zeroes the odd partner" [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2054-2061]. set_v (the cache method that writes one V row) zeroes the odd partner on the even path with _mm512_cvtepu16_epi32 [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2297-2303]. append_v (the cache method that copies one V row between pages) zeroes the odd partner on both even-destination paths [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1866-1920]. F28's source citations are correct.

Why the finding is refuted as a design finding:

- Every element F28 says the figure should show is already stated in the design's prose. Even writes zero the odd row: "Writing an even token clears the following odd token's row whenever the pair is reused" [design-text.txt:375], "Provide a form that adds an even token and zeros the odd row in the same pass" [330], "Keep clearing the odd row when writing an even destination token" [440]. Ordinary row assignment and odd appends must preserve the partner: "row.set(expr) ... Preserve the other row in its stored pair" [262], "Ordinary row assignment must preserve the other row in the pair. This applies even when the odd row is written first. It cannot use the current behavior of page::set_v(even)" [392], "Adding an odd token preserves the even row in its pair" [332]. The consumer that reads the padding slot: "When the number of used token positions in the page is odd, the weighted V sum also reads the following unused row. That row must contain zero values. A zero weight cannot prevent a NaN in that row from affecting the sum" [375]. Reused storage: the test row "Include reused storage and all even/odd append combinations" [518] and the separate test row for ordinary assignment "Write odd then even through .set(). Verify both rows and an untouched pair" [516].
- An implementing agent reading those sentences builds the right thing with or without a two-lane figure. Ben's comments #2 and #3 concern the C++ API (vnni_tensor, views, row load/store, storage construction, keeping V's zero-initialization invariant) and say nothing about the design page's figures [facts.md:28-29]. jhan's prompt asks for a design "another agent will implement ... by reading this file" [codex-add-tensor-type.md:27-28]. Neither yardstick is affected by diagram form.
- The verifier rule for this lens says to refute a finding that is a matter of taste with no consequence for the implementer or for Ben's acceptance. F28 fits that rule.

Two inaccuracies inside F28 itself:

- "the invariant the design calls trickiest": the design never uses "trickiest" or any equivalent word (grep for "trick" in the HTML returns nothing). The design lists the invariant first under section 6, nothing more. This phrase is unsupported.
- "The even -> completion -> odd diagram shows the ordinary order but not the invariant": diagram 3's boxes read "Write even row. Zero odd partner." and "Preserve even row. Write odd row." [html:275-279]. It does show the two write rules of the invariant. What it omits is the contrast case (row.set must preserve), the stale-row reuse case, and the consumer (the weighted V sum reading the padding slot).

Residual worth knowing (note level): a mechanism figure of the kind F28 recommends would match jhan's general preference for mechanism diagrams, and diagrams 1 and 2 add no information. That is an optional polish item for the page, not a change the implementer needs.

confirmed.title: Row chunk/set mechanics and override signature unspecified
confirmed.section: 5. Interface design - operations table (matrix[token].chunk(i), bf16_chunk(i), row.set(expr))
confirmed.claim: Ambiguity: the design requires vector extraction for chunk(i) and pair-preserving row.set(expr) but does not say how a chunk maps onto the packed pair or how the even/odd merge happens. The expr base detects an override by `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)` [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:110-117]. The stride-2 rank-1 view is a real type: operator[] returns *(data + i*s0) with s0 a template parameter [view.hpp:146-148].

If vnni_row declares a bf16_chunk whose parameter type, return type, or const-qualifier differs from the base, the two pointer-to-member types have no composite pointer type, so the comparison in the if-constexpr condition is ill-formed and the build fails; it does not fall back silently. A difference only in noexcept still forms a composite pointer type and the override is detected. It gives the address formula "(token / 2) * (2 * D) + 2 * dimension + token % 2" [design-text.txt:184], from which chunk i of token t is 32 contiguous bf16 at pair base + 32*i. It says vnni_row "stores the address of the first value in the token pair. It also stores whether its token is the even or odd member" [design-text.txt:242]. Step 2 says "Move the existing V packing, unpacking, and append conversion code. Preserve the single-pass even-token write. Section 6 says ordinary row assignment "cannot use the current behavior of page::set_v(even), which clears the odd row" [design-text.txt:392]. Those sentences point the implementer at the exact primitives F35 lists (scaled_v_expr::odd_part/even_part at kv_cache.hpp:1999-2006@f46e48bab498, the set_v odd path ternarylogic merge at kv_cache.hpp:2305-2320@f46e48bab498). The instruction-level recipe F35 asks for is implementation detail, not a design gap.

Part C (stride-2 view alternative not named): the design states the requirement that rules it out. "Extract the packed values with vector operations" [design-text.txt:258]; "Do not substitute: A loop that reads one scalar value at a time through the new row accessors" [design-text.txt:412]. I confirmed the alternative exists and is scalar: rank-1 view<T,aligned,dma,seq<d0>,sseq<s0>> with s0 != 1 gathers in chunk() [view.hpp:155-166@f46e48bab498] and stores scalar in set() [view.hpp:186-204@f46e48bab498], and the type is declared final [view.hpp:116@f46e48bab498] so it cannot be extended. F35 itself concedes the alternative is scalar, so it gives no evidence the design's choice is wrong. Naming the rejected alternative is a note, not a required change.

Part B (bf16_chunk override detection): this is a real omission, but F35 overstates the consequence. Verified: expr<B,N>::bf16_chunk dispatches with "if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)" [expr.hpp:109-116@f46e48bab498]. The two existing overriders both use the non-template form "bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept" [dmatensor.hpp:367-371@f46e48bab498 (with a requires clause); permuted.hpp:53@f46e48bab498]. A template or overloaded bf16_chunk makes "&B::bf16_chunk" ill-formed and the comparison fails to compile at the first use, which is loud, not silent. The silent fallback is bit-exact, not a numerics change: chunk(i) yields fp32 lanes with zero low 16 bits [bf16.hpp:45-49@f46e48bab498 and the even_part/odd_part forms], and fp32s_to_bf16s only alters bits when the low 16 bits are nonzero [bf16.hpp:92-109@f46e48bab498]. confirmed.section: 5. Interface design - Select rows and dimensions without assuming consecutive storage
confirmed.claim: Ambiguity: the design requires full-matrix set to initialize complete pairs without reading destination bytes and separately requires writable slices, including slices that start at an odd token. A slice whose first or last row is the odd or even half of a stored pair shares that pair with rows outside the slice, so a no-read pair store on the boundary pair would erase a neighbor. The design does not say that slice.set() must use the pair-preserving row path (or whole-pair stores only for interior complete pairs).

confirmed.title: Load side unnamed; Ben's store_row/load_row not mapped
confirmed.section: 5. Interface design; 6. Copy, append, and preparation for hardware

also.title: Ben's store_row/load_row not mapped to append_v_row, set_pair, chunk()
also.claim: Ambiguity: Ben asked for row-wise load/store operations named store_row, load_row and store_block. The design renames the store side to append_v_row plus set_pair, splits its semantics (row.set preserves the pair partner; append zeroes it), and gives the load side no name; loads appear only as matrix[token].chunk(i) and bf16_chunk(i) and as "Move the existing V packing, unpacking". The split is well argued in section 6 but is not presented as a change to Ben's single store_row. Reviewers cannot see at a glance that Ben's requirement is met, and the implementing agent must infer that the existing get_v loop (one 512-bit load per 16 dimensions, kv_cache.hpp:2408-2470) is the body chunk(i)/bf16_chunk(i) must reproduce.
also.evidence: Ben 5765866077 section 4: "store_row(...)", "load_row(...)", "Corresponding overloads for v_vnni_layout", "For V, the overloads contain the existing interleave/deinterleave operations". h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2408-2470@f46e48bab498 (get_v float and bf16: `for (i = 0; i < head_size; i += 16) { _mm512_load_si512(v_ptr + i * 2) ... }`). also.recommendation: Add a three-row mapping table: Ben store_row (V) -> append_v_row + set_pair (zeroes partner on even append) and row.set(expr) (preserves partner); Ben load_row (V) -> vnni_row::chunk(i) / bf16_chunk(i), whose per-16-dimension body is today's get_v loop [kv_cache.hpp:2408-2470]; Ben store_block (K) -> child only. State that both directions keep the existing instruction sequences.

confirmed.title: page::k_tensor duplicates page::k in the parent
confirmed.section: 5. Interface design - Page and kernel arguments that identify the layout
confirmed.claim: Design decision I disagree with: page::k_tensor<geometry>(slot, head) returns 'its existing row-major view', which is exactly what page::k<geometry>(slot, kv_head) returns today. A second name for the same view is a rename with no behavior, and the child would then have to constrain two K accessors instead of one for VNNI slots. Choosing the K view type by layout is a child concern; Ben's straw-man does it in kv_block with std::conditional_t.
confirmed.evidence: kv_cache.hpp:1547-1570 at f46e48bab498 (page::k returns `kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).k_view()`); kv_cache.hpp:2208-2220 (k_view returns view<bf16,true,false,seq<page_size,head_size>>). Child 30c4ac82cbb6 kv_cache.hpp diff: every page::k overload gains `!k_vnni::layout_on<...>` and k_vnni_plane is added. Ben #3 s5: `using k_storage = std::conditional_t<k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, vnni_tensor<...>, existing_row_major_k_storage>;`.
confirmed.design_quote: Add page::k_tensor<geometry>(slot, head) to provide a matrix view of K without copying its values. Native K returns its existing row-major view.
confirmed.recommendation: Drop page::k_tensor from the parent and keep page::k. Add only page::v_tensor (page::v already exists in the 8-lane build with a row signature, so keep the distinct name). Move 'layout-selected K accessor' to the 'Then update PR #4424' list.

votes.reason:
Core claim verified from primary sources; it holds.

(1) page::k returns the same view the design assigns to k_tensor. At f46e48bab498, h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp lines 1547-1570: every page::k(slot, kv_head) overload (uniform and <geometry>, mutable and const) returns `kv_block(...).k_view()`. Lines 2208-2220: kv_block::k_view() returns `view<bf16, true, false, seq<page_size, head_size>>` (const form: const_view of the same shape) via reinterpret_cast of the k array. The design's single mention of k_tensor (grep of the HTML: exactly 1 occurrence, section 5 "Page and kernel arguments that identify the layout") says verbatim: "Add page::k_tensor<geometry>(slot, head) to provide a matrix view of K without copying its values. Native K returns its existing row-major view." and two sentences later "Keep existing page methods where needed." No other rationale, contract, or migration instruction for k_tensor appears anywhere in the page. So in the parent PR, k_tensor and page::k return identical types from identical storage; the finding's "rename with no behavior" reading is what the text says.

(2) The design's own typed kernel boundary does not need k_tensor: it declares `qk_rowmajor_128x4(const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> k, ...)` with `const_native_k_view<Rows,Cols> = const_view<bf16,true,false,seq<Rows,Cols>>` (design section 5, "Owner, matrix view, and row expression" block). That is exactly the type `page::k<geometry>(slot, kv_head) const` already returns at f46e48ba. Existing callers at main (model.hpp:2757 `pg.template k<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, j).set(kout)`; self_attention.hpp:1423, 1545, 1580) can pass page::k unchanged.

(3) Child evidence verified: `git diff f46e48bab498 30c4ac82cbb6 -- h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp` shows all 8 page::k overloads gain `!k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>` / `!k_vnni::layout_on<geometry.head_size>` in their requires clauses, and adds `k_vnni_plane<geometry>()` (const bf16*, requires layout_on), set_k_row, get_k_row, set_k_block. Child call sites (model.hpp/self_attention.hpp/full.hpp diff) use set_k_row/set_k_block/k_vnni_plane/get_k_row, not a renamed page::k.

(4) Ben #3 (github-review.json body, section 5) verbatim: `using k_storage = std::conditional_t<k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, vnni_tensor<k_vnni_layout<page_size, head_size>>, existing_row_major_k_storage>; k_storage k;` inside kv_block, plus a page accessor `k_packed(...)` returning `kv_block<geometry>(slot, head).k.as_view()`. Ben selects the K type at the storage level and adds a distinct accessor only for the packed case; he does not rename the native-K accessor. This matches the finding's recommendation (keep page::k, no alias in the parent).

(5) Recommendation's premise about page::v verified: at f46e48ba kv_cache.hpp lines 1674-1720, `page::v(slot, kv_head, i_page)` exists only under `#else // TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16` and returns a rank-1 row view `view<bf16,true,false,seq<head_size>>`; the CHUNK 16 branch has set_v/get_v/v_data and no page::v. So "v_tensor" as a distinct name for a matrix accessor is justified, and the asymmetry (add v_tensor, skip k_tensor) is sound.

Not refuted. Kind (b) design disagreement, minor severity, is the right classification: the parent is not wrong to compile with an alias, but the design gives no reason for it and Ben's precedent does not include it.

Two sub-points need adjusting, without changing the verdict.

With a parent-side k_tensor alias, the child must constrain page::k (8 overloads, as 30c4ac82cbb6 already does) and turn k_tensor into the layout-selecting accessor. Without the alias, the child must constrain page::k and add a layout-selecting accessor. The child work is the same in both cases; the objection is only that the parent carries a purposeless second name, not that the child does extra work.

(b) The recommendation "Move 'layout-selected K accessor' to the 'Then update PR #4424' list" is partly already satisfied: that list already contains "Select the K owner and view using the existing conditions on storage geometry." confirmed.title: std::start_lifetime_as not implemented in pinned toolchain
confirmed.section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve - Storage and how long its objects remain valid
confirmed.claim: Factual gap: the "supported C++23 function for starting object lifetimes" is std::start_lifetime_as (P2590R2). The repository pins Clang 19 (llvm19.stdenv) with GNU libstdc++ and -std=c++23. libstdc++ through GCC 15 and libc++ through LLVM 20 list P2590R2 as not implemented, so the option the design offers is not available (vendor status pages; the implementer should re-check in the pinned nix store, as the design already asks). confirmed.claim: Omission: the design says the two conversions 'handle NaN differently' but does not state the rule, while its test row asks for independently chosen expected bits for NaN and infinity. The design's description of the set_v path (convert to fp32, keep the upper 16 bits) is confirmed correct. The exact divergence is this: for an fp32 input whose exponent field is all ones and whose low 16 bits are nonzero, set_v keeps the upper 16 bits unchanged, so a NaN whose upper 7 mantissa bits are zero becomes +/-Inf (0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F80). fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic conversion in simd/bf16.hpp) first ORs 0x00010000 into such inputs, so the result is always a NaN (0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F81). Infinity, denormal and finite inputs convert identically in both paths (truncation, no rounding, no flush to zero). The fp16 path has the same property after cvtph_ps (fp16 0x7C01 becomes fp32 0x7F802000, then set_v gives 0x7F80 = +Inf and the generic path gives 0x7F81). In the 8-lane build the row-view .set() path uses fp32s_to_bf16s, so the two builds legitimately give different bits for those inputs, and the test's expected values must be chosen per build.

The design states the mechanism ("The existing conversion to fp32 followed by keeping its upper 16 bits") but never states the observable consequence, while its test row asks for independently chosen NaN/Inf expected bits. INTENT lens: neither Ben (#2/#3) nor jhan's prompt mentions conversion numerics, but the issue body and the design itself make "preserve conversions" a requirement, so spelling out the rule serves that stated intent rather than pushing away from it. The fp16 worked example is wrong in its outcome. set_v uses the hardware instruction VCVTPH2PS (`_mm512_cvtph_ps`, kv_cache.hpp:2340@f46e48bab498). Per the Intel SDM (Vol 1 section 4.8.3.4, Table 4-7; VCVTPH2PS lists the Invalid exception), a signaling NaN source is returned as its quiet form when the exception is masked, so fp16 0x7C01 becomes fp32 0x7FC02000, not 0x7F802000. Every fp16 NaN therefore reaches fp32 with bit 22 set, and set_v truncation yields 0x7FC0 (a NaN), never +Inf. The fp16 divergence is only the low bit: set_v gives 0x7FC0, the generic conversion gives 0x7FC1 (low 16 bits 0x2000 are nonzero, so 0x00010000 is ORed in). The per-build statement about expected values (8-lane follows fp32s_to_bf16s, 16-lane follows truncation) stands.

confirmed.title: Typed kernel parameters pull SIMD headers into intrinsics-free header
confirmed.section: 7. Implementation steps - Step 6 Attention callers
confirmed.claim: Omission: amx_attn_iface.hpp documents itself as containing no intrinsics so any translation unit may include it, and self_attention.hpp includes it with an "intrinsics-free" comment. Typing its parameters with vnni_view and const_native_k_view requires either including the new tensor header (which includes view.hpp and therefore tron/simd.hpp with AVX intrinsics) or forward declarations. The design does not say which. Forward declarations suffice for function declarations with by-value parameters, and expr.hpp already forward-declares view and const_view as precedent.

confirmed.design_quote: 6. Attention callers | h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp, h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp, and src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp | Use typed native-K and packed-V kernel parameters.
confirmed.recommendation: Add to Step 6: forward-declare `template <typename T, size_t R, size_t D> class vnni_view;` and the view/const_view/seq templates in amx_attn_iface.hpp instead of including the tensor header, so the header stays intrinsics-free; include the full headers only in amx_attn.cpp and the fake TUs.

The cited lines exist as quoted, but the finding misreads what "intrinsics-free" protects, and its recommendation would not compile as written.

1. "No intrinsics" in amx_attn_iface.hpp means AMX intrinsics that need the -mamx-* compile flags, not AVX intrinsics. The header comment ties the statement to "-mamx-tile/-mamx-bf16" [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:2-5@f46e48bab498]. The build file says the same: "The kernel bodies live in one isolated translation unit that alone receives the -mamx-* flags; the rest of the tree sees only the intrinsics-free interface header" [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:184-187@f46e48bab498]. AVX and AVX-512 flags are PUBLIC compile options of the tron target, so every translation unit that can include this header already compiles AVX intrinsics [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:243-246@f46e48bab498].

2. Every current includer of amx_attn_iface.hpp already sees tron/simd.hpp. self_attention.hpp includes dotter.hpp, expr.hpp and kv_cache.hpp right after the iface header [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:21-27@f46e48bab498]; expr.hpp itself includes tron/simd/bf16.hpp, fp16.hpp, fp32.hpp, int4.hpp [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:8-12@f46e48bab498]. t_amx_numerics.cpp includes dotter.hpp [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:27@f46e48bab498]. t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp includes model.hpp [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:41@f46e48bab498]. amx_attn.cpp includes <immintrin.h> [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:8@f46e48bab498]. Including the new tensor header from the iface header therefore adds no SIMD exposure to any translation unit, and "any translation unit may include it" stays true. The expr.hpp "precedent" is for circular-dependency avoidance (its own comment, expr.hpp:17), in a header full of SIMD includes, so it is not a precedent for keeping a header SIMD-free.

3. The recommendation "forward-declare ... the view/const_view/seq templates" is not implementable as stated. seq is an alias template (`template <size_t... ds> using seq = std::integer_sequence<size_t, ds...>;`) [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp:22-23@f46e48bab498]; alias templates cannot be forward-declared, so seq.hpp must be included (it is SIMD-free: seq.hpp:3-9). The design's 4-argument alias `const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<Rows, Cols>>` (design section 5) relies on the default `Stride = row_major<Dim>` declared at [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:22-27 and 31-36@f46e48bab498]. A forward declaration without that default, parsed before views.hpp as in self_attention.hpp's include order (iface at line 21, view headers at 22-27), makes the 4-argument template-id ill-formed (too few arguments). Repeating the default in the forward declaration is also ill-formed: a template parameter may not be given a default argument by two declarations in the same scope ([temp.param]/12).

4. What remains true: the design does not state whether amx_attn_iface.hpp includes the tensor header or forward-declares the types (design-text step 6, line 464; step 1 only says "The tensor header must not include an attention kernel header.", line 454; section 8 lists "Unwanted header dependencies" as a failure the three-configuration build detects, line 526). But the natural choice (include the tensor header) compiles within the documented contract and creates no cycle, because step 1 already forbids the reverse direction. An implementing agent would not build the wrong thing. This is a note, not an omission requiring a design change.

confirmed.title: 8-lane and other build configurations lack flags and CI lane
confirmed.section: 8. Verification and acceptance (Parent build configurations; Missing parent CI evidence)
confirmed.claim: Omission: the design requires building and testing the 8-lane row-major V configuration but does not say that no CI job at the reviewed main builds it, how to build it, or whether unmodified main compiles in it. TRON_CHUNK_SIZE (the number of fp32 lanes per vector) is 16 exactly when TRON_AVX512_ENABLED is defined, and the CMake option AVX512 (default ON) defines it. The Nix CI build passes -DAVX512=ON. The manual CMake workflow uses preset native on runners labeled avx512, and the host probe only ever turns AVX512 OFF when a CPU feature is missing. The only preset with AVX512 OFF is darwin, selected by the GNUmakefile on macOS only, and no workflow file mentions it. The design's 'Missing parent CI evidence' paragraph covers the AMX gap only.

also.evidence: h/tron/simd/auto.hpp@f46e48bab498 lines 17-21: TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 16 under TRON_AVX512_ENABLED, else 8. src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@f46e48bab498 lines 244-246: if(AVX512) adds -mavx512* and defines TRON_AVX512_ENABLED; line 193-197: if(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) compiles kernels/amx_attn.cpp and defines TRON_AMX_DISPATCH. CMakeLists.txt@f46e48bab498 line 44 option(AVX512 ON), line 48 option(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH OFF). h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@f46e48bab498 lines 30-35: '#error TRON_AMX_DISPATCH requires TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16'. CMakePresets.json@98bb8cb22f94: presets native and cross-avx512 set AVX512 ON; only darwin sets AVX512 OFF. nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix line 88: -DAVX512=ON. Design text never contains the strings TRON_CHUNK_SIZE or TRON_AMX_DISPATCH.
also.recommendation: Add a three-row table: (1) cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF (TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 16; the required Nix CI build); (2) cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON (the manual CMake workflow); (3) cmake --preset native -DAVX512=OFF (TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 8; AMX cannot be combined, per the #error at self_attention.hpp:30-35). State that no CI lane builds (3) today and whether (3) is build-only or build-and-test, and on which host.

votes.reason: Every cited source line holds at f46e48bab498. h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17-21 reads `#if defined(TRON_AVX512_ENABLED) / #define TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 16 / #else / #define TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 8`. src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:244-246 reads `if(AVX512)` ... `target_compile_definitions(tron PUBLIC TRON_AVX512_ENABLED)`. CMakeLists.txt:44 reads `option(AVX512 "Enable AVX512" ON)`, and the BUILD_NATIVE probe at CMakeLists.txt:95-117 only executes `set(AVX512 OFF)` when a required feature is missing from lscpu output. nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:86-88 passes `-DBUILD_NATIVE=OFF` and `-DAVX512=ON` (flake.nix:1206-1208 does the same for the sandbox-configure check). .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:151 has `runs-on: [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]` and :353-355 runs `cmake ... --preset native ... -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON`. CMakePresets.json:49-66 defines preset "darwin" with `"AVX512": "OFF"`, the only preset that does so; GNUmakefile:216-218 selects it only when `uname -s` is Darwin. `git grep -i "avx512\|darwin\|preset" f46e48bab498 -- .github nix` returns only avx512 runner labels, the preset-native line, and the Nix `-DAVX512=ON`; no workflow sets AVX512=OFF or uses the darwin preset. h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:30-35 has `#error "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH requires TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 ..."`, so the 8-lane configuration cannot be combined with AMX. On the design side, plain grep of status/design-new-tensor-type.html finds 0 occurrences of "AVX512", "TRON_CHUNK_SIZE" and "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH"; the only 8-lane mentions are the storage sentence (HTML line 301) and the quoted acceptance row (line 370), and the "Missing parent CI evidence" paragraph (line 383) speaks only about the Nix build leaving AMX disabled. One nuance that does not refute the finding: cpp-coverage.yml (weekly schedule + manual dispatch, runs-on [self-hosted, fpga, test] without the avx512 label) runs `cmake --preset coverage` (GNUmakefile:609), which leaves BUILD_NATIVE ON and lets the host probe decide, so it could produce an 8-lane build by accident on a runner without AVX-512; it never selects that configuration deliberately and is not among the required checks listed in README.ci.md:74-77. Whether any such runner exists is Insufficient data (would need the runner inventory).

The finding's evidence holds at f46e48bab498 and the design does not cover the gap elsewhere.

Evidence checked in the source (all at f46e48bab498):
- h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17-21: TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 16 when TRON_AVX512_ENABLED is defined, else 8.
- src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:244-247: `if(AVX512)` adds the -mavx512* flags and defines TRON_AVX512_ENABLED.
- CMakeLists.txt:44: `option(AVX512 "Enable AVX512" ON)`. CMakeLists.txt:95-117: the BUILD_NATIVE probe only ever runs `set(AVX512 OFF)` (line 112) when a feature is missing.
- nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:88 and flake.nix:1208 both pass `-DAVX512=ON`, so every Nix CI build is 16-lane.
- .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:151/381/511 run on `[self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]` and line 353 configures `--preset native`, so the manual lane is 16-lane too.
- CMakePresets.json:50-64: only preset `darwin` sets `"AVX512": "OFF"`. GNUmakefile:217-218 selects it only on macOS. `git grep 'AVX512\|darwin' f46e48bab498 -- .github` returns nothing, so no workflow builds with AVX512 off.
- h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:30-35: `#error "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH requires TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16"`, confirming the 8-lane configuration cannot be combined with AMX (R62's point).
- The TRON_CHUNK_UNSUPPORTED static_asserts (expr.hpp, int4.hpp, permuted.hpp, quantization.hpp, safetensors.hpp) all sit in `#else` branches after `#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 8 / #elif == 16`, so they do not prove the 8-lane build is broken; whether unmodified main compiles at AVX512=OFF is Insufficient data without a build, which is exactly what the finding says the design leaves open.

Design-text fairness check (whole design-text.txt read):
- The strings AVX512, TRON_AVX512_ENABLED, TRON_CHUNK_SIZE, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, darwin, and preset appear nowhere in the design text or the HTML markup (grep on design-new-tensor-type.html returned nothing). The only CMake option the design links is CMakeLists.txt#L48 (TRON_AMX_DISPATCH), not line 44 (AVX512).
- The "Parent build configurations" row (design line 526) names the three configurations in words only and lists "a fallback configuration that no longer compiles" as the failure it detects, which presupposes that the 8-lane build compiles on main today; the design gives no evidence for that.
- "Missing parent CI evidence" (line 546) covers only the AMX-off Nix build, as the finding says.
- The design defers build commands to the run-tron-tests skill (line 534), but that skill's text contains no AVX, preset, or configuration guidance (it is about routing to Dice hosts). README.ci.md:550-556 describes the native and cross-avx512 presets but does not say how to get a Linux AVX512=OFF build.
- The design is not flagging the omission as a deliberate choice, so the "deliberate choice" refutation rule does not apply.

Partial coverage: design lines 540 ("Name every skipped check and its reason") and 566 ("Name every hardware or build-configuration check that was not run") already require the implementer to list an unrun 8-lane build. So the last sentence of the finding's recommendation is redundant with the design. The rest of the finding stands.
votes.correction: The finding holds except for one redundant sentence in its recommendation. Keep: the design names the 8-lane row-major V configuration as a required build-and-test target (line 526) without naming the option that selects it (AVX512=OFF, which makes TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 8 via TRON_AVX512_ENABLED), without saying that no CI job at f46e48bab498 builds it (Nix and the manual CMake lane both force AVX512 ON; only the macOS-only darwin preset turns it off), and without saying whether unmodified main compiles in it. Drop from the recommendation: "If this build was not done, list it under checks not run." The design already requires that at lines 540 and 566 ("Name every hardware or build-configuration check that was not run"). Add to the recommendation: the 8-lane configuration cannot be combined with TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON, per the #error at h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:30-35 at f46e48bab498, so the three configurations are exactly (AVX512=ON, AMX off), (AVX512=ON, AMX on), and (AVX512=OFF, AMX off).

votes.reason: I checked every cited source at f46e48bab498 and all of it holds. h/tron/simd/auto.hpp:17-21 defines TRON_CHUNK_SIZE 16 under TRON_AVX512_ENABLED and 8 otherwise. src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:244-247 defines TRON_AVX512_ENABLED only under if(AVX512). CMakeLists.txt:44 declares option(AVX512 "Enable AVX512" ON), and the BUILD_NATIVE probe at CMakeLists.txt:96-116 only ever executes set(AVX512 OFF) when an lscpu feature is missing. nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:86-88 passes -DBUILD_NATIVE=OFF -DAVX512=ON, so the required GCP Nix "Build Tron"/"Test host" checks (README.ci.md:74-78) never build the 8-lane variant. .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:151 runs the build job on [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512] and line 353 configures with --preset native, so the probe keeps AVX512 ON there too. CMakePresets.json: only the darwin preset sets "AVX512": "OFF"; native, cross-avx512, deb, asan, tsan, coverage all leave it ON or default ON. GNUmakefile:216-218 selects darwin only when uname is Darwin; on a non-AVX-512 Linux host it selects cross-avx512 (AVX512 ON, compile-only) rather than an 8-lane build, and the Note [Cross-Compile for AVX-512] at GNUmakefile:986-994 confirms this is deliberate. A git grep for "darwin" or "AVX512=OFF" over .github at f46e48bab498 returns nothing; the only .github matches for avx512 are runner labels. kv_cache.hpp:2195-2201 does keep an 8-lane `#else` V branch, so the configuration exists in the code, and the design's acceptance row at design-text line 526 requires it be built and tested ("Build and test three supported configurations: ... and 8-lane row-major V"). The design page contains no occurrence of TRON_CHUNK_SIZE, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, AVX512, or a preset name (grep of the HTML), and its "Missing parent CI evidence" paragraph (design-text line 546) speaks only of AMX being disabled in the Nix build. Intent lens: Ben's comments #2/#3 say nothing about build configurations, and jhan's prompt says "Another agent will implement the design by reading this file", so adding the build flags and the CI-coverage gap serves the handoff without moving the design away from either intent. It is not a matter of taste: the design's own definition of done says "Name every hardware or build-configuration check that was not run", and an implementer cannot do that for the 8-lane build without knowing how it is selected and that no CI job exercises it. The recommended command (cmake --preset native -DAVX512=OFF) is valid because the probe can only turn AVX512 off, never back on. Consequence is limited to an implementer having to look these facts up or skipping the 8-lane build unnoticed, so minor is the right severity.

confirmed.title: Guard paragraph mislabels lib-guard.sh; half-machine rule omitted
confirmed.section: 8. Verification and acceptance (Where to build and run tests)
confirmed.claim: Factual error and omission: the design calls lib-guard.sh (the user's shared launch-guard script for delphi-3bda) "the script that reserves the host". The script does not reserve the host against CI; it checks the CI lease file, which is authoritative, and refuses or waits. It also takes a file lock only among the user's own campaigns. The paragraph names no function to call and leaves out the half-machine rule (second socket only, marker file /bill-has-instance-0,2 for the other user) and the rule that whole-machine measurements need jhan's approval.

Cross-session campaign flock /var/tmp/jhan/3bda-campaign.lock', '3. The clock window ... ADVISORY only', '4. Other people'); functions ci_lease_busy (line 25), other_user_active (60), campaign_guard_acquire (146), blackout_active (306), ci_took_dut (316), wait_for_dut_free (321). ~/workspace/notebook/handoffs/check-CI.md 'Short version': the lease file 'is the only reliable "CI is running right now" signal, so check it instead of the clock.' confirmed.design_quote: Before a series of test runs on that host, apply the user’s rule for detecting an active CI lease. Acquire the campaign guard from ~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/lib-guard.sh, the script that reserves the host for the run. Check again between long runs whether CI has taken the host.
confirmed.recommendation: Rewrite: "Source ~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/lib-guard.sh. Call campaign_guard_acquire before the first run; it refuses when the CI lease is busy (ci_lease_busy), another person is active (other_user_active) or a blackout window is set (blackout_active). Re-check ci_took_dut between runs and stop when it returns 0. Stay on the second socket; bin/slice bench runs on both sockets and needs jhan's go-ahead. Never run a real-driver tron binary on delphi-3bda without --instance." Cite notebook handoffs/check-CI.md and delphi-3bda-guard.md.

votes.reason: The finding holds. (1) The design quote is verbatim at design-text.txt line 538: "Acquire the campaign guard from ~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/lib-guard.sh, the script that reserves the host for the run." (2) lib-guard.sh header lines 5-12 list the authority order: "1. CI lease /run/lock/systems-test-ci.lease - AUTHORITATIVE" and "2. Cross-session campaign flock /var/tmp/jhan/3bda-campaign.lock". campaign_guard_acquire (lines 146-179) only READS the lease via ci_lease_busy and returns 1 with "GUARD: System CI holds the DUT (lease busy)"; the flock it takes is on a file under /var/tmp/jhan/, and check-CI.md lines 39-40 say "Our campaigns take one lock on /var/tmp/jhan/3bda-campaign.lock, so only one campaign runs per machine". Nothing in the script makes CI or another user honor that lock, so "reserves the host" is not what it does against CI. (3) The function names and line numbers in the finding match exactly: ci_lease_busy 25, other_user_active 60, campaign_guard_acquire 146, blackout_active 306, ci_took_dut 316, wait_for_dut_free 321. The design paragraph names none of them. (4) Omission confirmed: a grep of the whole design text for "instance", "socket", "bill", "half", "whole machine", "marker", "slice bench" finds nothing (only "bin/slice route" at line 534). Memory 3bda-shared-with-bill.md (UPDATE 2026-09-06 22:25 and 2026-09-15) states: our half = socket 1 = SYSTEM_CONFIG="--instance 1,2", marker /bill-has-instance-0,2 = Bill may use the first half, "Whole-machine work only after jhan says so", "bin/slice bench --update launches tests under --instance i,n for every slot (both sockets), so it is a whole-machine measurement", and "never run a real-driver tron binary on 3bda without --instance (deletes unlocked slice files)". notebook handoffs/delphi-3bda-guard.md exists and its Short version gives Rule 2 "use only the second half". The omission matters to the design's own step "Update Slice's recorded test durations" (design-text.txt line 544), which is the whole-machine bin/slice bench run. (5) check-CI.md Short version quote matches: "that lease file is the only reliable \"CI is running right now\" signal, so check it instead of the clock."
votes.correction: Two small adjustments. First, "factual error" overstates the first point: the flock in campaign_guard_acquire does reserve the machine among jhan's own campaign sessions (lib-guard.sh lines 11-12, 155-160), so "the script that reserves the host" is imprecise and misleading about CI rather than flatly false; label it "misleading wording" and keep the rest of the finding (no function named; half-machine rule, marker file, and jhan-approval rule omitted) as omissions. Second, the recommendation's list of refusal conditions is incomplete: campaign_guard_acquire also refuses when a runtron process is already running (lines 165-170, "GUARD: runtron already running") and when rinzler serving is active unless the caller passes --allow-serving (lines 175-179); the rewrite should name both.

That skill at f46e48ba contains no delphi-3bda sharing or --instance rule (grep: no hits), so the deferral does not cover the split. votes.reason: I checked the finding's evidence and it holds. (1) Mislabel: the design's bullet reads "Acquire the campaign guard from ~/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/lib-guard.sh, the script that reserves the host for the run" [design-new-tensor-type.html, section 8 "Where to build and run tests", third <li>]. lib-guard.sh describes itself as "Shared launch guards for AMX campaigns on delphi-3bda" and states the authority order: "1. confirmed.title: Formatting, IWYU and benchmark-refresh commands not named
confirmed.section: 8. Verification and acceptance (Where to build and run tests)
confirmed.claim: Omission: the design asks for "the C++ formatting command and required static checks" and "the repository's documented process" for test durations without naming them. The repository names them: make format, make iwyu-check (required when a public API header changes, which this parent does), make build-test, make test-host, and bin/slice bench --update <name>.

votes.reason: The omission is real. The design text contains no "make ", "bin/slice bench", "iwyu" or "clang-format" (grep of design-text.txt: the only command it names is "bin/slice route", line 534). It delegates by name to the run-tron-tests skill (design lines 534, 540, 544) and links that skill, AGENTS.md and t/AGENTS.md under S12 (design-new-tensor-type.html lines 469-471). The finding's cited evidence holds verbatim at 98bb8cb22f94: .agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md lines 55-56 ("`h/`, `src/`, or C++ tests: build and run `t_<name>`, then run `make build-test` and `make test-host`."), 65-66 ("A public API header: run the affected test and `make iwyu-check`, then `make build-test` and `make test-host`."), 69-70 ("New or materially changed tests require `bin/slice bench --new` or `bin/slice bench --update <name>` after the test passes."); GNUmakefile targets lint:693, format:819, iwyu-check:984; t/AGENTS.md lines 23-25 ("After adding or materially changing a test, refresh `config/test-benchmarks.json` with `bin/slice bench --new` or targeted `bin/slice bench --update <name>`."). README.ci.md:657-660 also names the local reproduction as `make build-test`, `make format`, `make lint`. The design's phrase "required static checks" is ambiguous because the repo has two different sets (make lint is a required CI check per README.ci.md:93; make iwyu-check applies only to a "public API header" per SKILL.md:65), and the design does not say which applies. Two sub-claims in the recommendation are wrong or incomplete, corrected below.

confirmed.section: 4. Keep token and dimension indexing unchanged

Inside each 16-token x 32-dimension tile, however, K is exactly the transposed packed-V formula (pairs of adjacent dimensions share a dword the way pairs of adjacent tokens do in V). Stating this helps the implementer see which pair helpers can be shared between vnni_view and k_vnni_view.

(2) k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:101-107 defines index(token, dim) = (((s*4 + c)*16 + dp)*16 + t)*2 + j with s = dim/32, c = token/16, dp = (dim%32)/2, t = token%16, j = dim%2. I enumerated all 64 x 128 = 8192 positions against the design's packed-V formula (token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2 with token and dimension exchanged over the whole plane (rows = 128 dims, cols = 64 tokens): 7680 mismatches, 512 matches. That reproduces the finding's number, so the design sentence is correct because of "alone". (3) Tile-wise: with tile base (s*4 + c)*512 and the transposed packed-V formula applied inside the tile (rows = 32 dims, cols = 16 tokens), all 8192 positions match. The same result follows from the byte-address code, not only from index(): pair_base (k_vnni.hpp:113-123) places token t at dword (s*4 + c)*256 + t and pair_row_offsets (126-132) steps the 16 pair rows by 16 dwords, so the local element index is dp*32 + 2*t + j, identical to (d/2)*(2*16) + 2*t + d%2 for d = 2*dp + j. (4) The dword-sharing statement holds: k_vnni.hpp:46-47 "The two values of one dimension pair share one 32-bit lane"; j = dim%2 is the innermost term. (5) The design does not state the per-tile relation anywhere (grep of design-text.txt for panel/tile/16 tokens/32 dimensions hits only lines 31, 188, 488); line 488 says "Keep the blocked K mapping inside this view. Keep it separate from packed V's mapping.", so the recommended sentence adds a fact and contradicts no design decision. (6) Recommended wording "tiles laid out dimension-step major, token-block minor" matches the tile base (s*4 + c)*512 with s = dimension step and c = token block (k_vnni.hpp:22-27 header comment). confirmed.title: kv_block size and alignment constraints hold with alignas(64) owner
confirmed.section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve (Storage and how long its objects remain valid)

confirmed.title: 'Extra EAGLE region' names two different buffers; only one holds kv_blocks
confirmed.section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve - Storage and how long its objects remain valid; 1. Words used here (EAGLE row)
confirmed.claim: Ambiguity: EAGLE (the speculative draft model that shares the cache) adds two extra things to a book (the object that owns the cache arenas), and the design's sentence "Cover every slot geometry and the extra EAGLE region" does not say which one it means. The first extra is one more KV storage slot with the primary geometry, appended to the retained arena; it holds kv_blocks (the K-plus-V storage of one head of one page) and needs the typed-storage construction. The second extra is a separate DMA buffer x_data of x_bytes per token that holds embedding bytes and no kv_block; constructing kv_blocks there would be wrong. Because EAGLE requires uniform geometry, a single array construction over the whole retained arena already covers the extra slot; the design does not say this either. The design also says the book owns "both byte arenas"; with EAGLE on it owns three DMA buffers.

The extra physical storage has no logical descriptor." (storage_slot_count = logical + 1); :714-721 arena_sizes adds `offsets.values[1].total()` to `result.retained` when support_eagle; :811-812 "Retained KV, reclaimable KV, and EAGLE embeddings are separate buffers"; :1106-1112 `x = hardware::try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite<uint8_t[]>(x_storage_bytes_)` stored in x_data; :1171-1175 x_storage_bytes = n_pages * page_size * x_bytes; :1744-1757 page embedding accessors read `book.x_data->get() + (pageno() * page_size + i_page) * x_bytes`; :1326-1329 kv_block_at_storage asserts "EAGLE geometry must match cache slot zero".

confirmed.title: Construction pass needs the slot-spec loop; allocate_kv_group has only a byte count
confirmed.section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve - Storage and how long its objects remain valid
confirmed.claim: Note (refines the panel's F12 recommendation): F12 names book::allocate_kv_group as the single place to construct the typed kv_block arrays, but that function receives only (reclaimable, bytes) and returns early when bytes is 0. For a heterogeneous layout each storage slot has its own geometry and its own byte offset inside the arena, so the construction pass must loop over the layout's slot specs and use layout_t::storage_location (which gives the arena and byte offset of a storage slot) to place one kv_block<page_size, geometry.head_size> array of n_kv_heads * n_pages elements per slot. For the uniform case one array over the whole arena suffices. The design's "Cover every slot geometry" is right but gives the agent none of these hooks.

confirmed.design_quote: Create these typed arrays on initial allocation and when restoring a released arena. Cover every slot geometry and the extra EAGLE region. Do this once per allocation.
confirmed.recommendation: Add: "Construction helper: after allocate_kv_group succeeds, for each storage slot whose storage_location names this arena, default-construct kv_block<page_size, spec.geometry.head_size>[n_kv_heads * n_pages] at arena + n_pages * byte_offset; in the uniform-geometry case this is one array over the whole arena. Skip arenas with 0 bytes."

The uniform-reclaimability path indexes blocks[(slot.i * n_kv_heads + kv_head) * n_pages + pg] over kv_blocks_alias [:1276-1290]. Heterogeneous layouts really do give each slot its own geometry and its own arena offset: kv_slot_spec carries a kv_geometry {n_kv_heads, head_size} per slot [:104-109, :154-159], and make_kv_slot_offsets accumulates slot_bytes = n_kv_heads * 2 * 64 * sizeof(bf16) * head_size per slot into per-arena prefix offsets [:646-672]. The design text names none of these hooks: a grep of design-new-tensor-type.html for allocate_kv_group, storage_location, slot_base, kv_block_at_storage, refresh_kv_blocks_alias, slot_specs and storage_slot_count returns zero hits; the design only links S8 to the regions kv_cache.hpp#L1187-, #L1274- and #L946-. I could not check the panel's F12 text (not supplied), so the sentence about F12 is unverified but not load-bearing.
