rejected.title: Generic writes into packed V have no caller or initializer
rejected.section: 5. Interface design - Owner, matrix view, and row expression; Separate adding cache rows from ordinary assignment
rejected.claim: Design decision I disagree with: the design adds four write paths into packed V with no caller: row.set(expr) that preserves the partner token, set_pair(pair_index, even_expr, odd_expr), matrix.set(expr), and an owner constructor and assignment from a matrix expression. Production code writes packed V in exactly two places, save_v_impl (one token from a raw row pointer) and append_v (one token, packed to packed), and both are covered by store_row and a token copy. The partner-preserving rule is new behavior. Today every even-token write zeroes the odd partner, and Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] names that as the invariant scaled_v relies on. The design itself says the preserving path may only run on already initialized pairs. Two write rules side by side, one of them without a caller, invite a later caller to use the preserving one on fresh storage and put indeterminate bytes next to a live token.
rejected.evidence: kv_cache.hpp:2296-2303 at f46e48bab498 (set_v even path: `_mm512_cvtepu16_epi32` zero-extends, comment 'cvtepu16_epi32 zeros the odd partner'); kv_cache.hpp:1868-1871 ('Even-destination paths zero the odd partner instead of preserving it. This is safe because append_v is only called via copy_from in append(), where destinations are always fresh ranges'); kv_cache.hpp:2055-2066 Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] ('Invariant: every even-indexed V write zeroes the odd partner'). model.hpp:2818 `pg.template set_v<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, j, &vs[ix][kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size])`. No call in h/ src/ t/ constructs tensor<64,D> (tensor.hpp:272) or dtensor (hardware/tensor.hpp:379) from a cache plane, and none assigns an expression into one (grep of set_v/get_v/v_data/v_ptr/scaled_v/.v[ at both commits lists only the callers named above).
rejected.design_quote: row.set(expr) | Write the logical row. Preserve the other row in its stored pair. [...] destination_view.set_pair(pair_index, even_row_expr, odd_row_expr); [...] Owner expression constructor / assignment | Accept a compatible matrix expression. [...] Ordinary row assignment reads and updates a pair, so that pair must already be initialized.
rejected.recommendation: Remove row.set(expr), set_pair, matrix.set(expr), and the owner expression constructor/assignment from the interface list, and remove the 'Ordinary row assignment' verification row. State one rule: 'The parent has one row write operation, store_row, with the semantics page::set_v has today: an even token zeroes its odd partner, an odd token merges into the pair.' Keep element writes via view[token][dim] for tests. If Ben later asks for expression assignment, add it in a follow-up with a caller and its own test.

also.title: Who initializes a pair before ordinary assignment is unnamed
also.claim: Ambiguity: the design says the pair 'must already be initialized' but names no party that guarantees it and names no production caller of packed ordinary row assignment. Arena bytes are never written at allocation: try_make_unique_dma_for_overwrite (the arena allocator) constructs elements only for non-trivially-constructible types, and bf16 is trivially constructible with an indeterminate __bf16 member. Reading an indeterminate scalar __bf16 is undefined behavior in the C++ abstract machine. The existing odd-token path instead reads the untouched even half through one 64-byte integer vector load, and two existing tests already do that on never-written storage. The design should say which read form the new row operations must use.
also.evidence: h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp:13,21@f46e48bab498: `__bf16 content;` and `constexpr bf16() noexcept = default;` with the comment "Constructed this way `content` has indeterminate state." h/system/memory.hpp:333-335@f46e48bab498: `if constexpr (not std::is_trivially_constructible_v<U>) ... new (array + i) U;` (the uint8_t arena is left as allocated). kv_cache.hpp:1199-1203: allocate_kv_group uses that allocator. kv_cache.hpp:2312: `bf16x32 even = _mm512_load_si512(v_ptr + i * 2);` (odd path reads the even half as a vector). t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2375: `dst_page.set_v(..., 7, nan_buf)` writes odd token 7 on a fresh book where even token 6 was never written; t_llama_unit.cpp:2462: writes odd slot 1 before even slot 0.
also.recommendation: Add: "The caller guarantees initialization. In the parent PR the only readers of a possibly unwritten pair half are the odd-token append and the tests at t_llama_unit.cpp:2375 and 2462. Both read the pair through one whole 64-byte integer vector load, as kv_cache.hpp:2312 does today, never through scalar bf16 element reads. row.set() on packed V must read the pair the same way." List the callers the parent touches (model.hpp:2818, self_attention.hpp:1451, full.hpp:2654, and the tests) so the statement 'no production caller of ordinary assignment' is checkable.

votes.reason: Premises verified at f46e48bab498. (1) The design lists row.set(expr), set_pair, matrix.set(expr) and an owner expression constructor/assignment (design-text.txt lines 262, 264, 272, 324-328). (2) Production writes into the packed V array happen in exactly two places: page::set_v called from save_v_impl [h/tron/models/model.hpp:2818] and append_v called from copy_storage_slot [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1945; body 1873-1920]. Under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 there is no memcpy or memset into packed V (the V memcpy at 1948-1955 is the CHUNK 8 branch). git grep over h/ src/ t/ finds no tensor constructed from a V plane and no expression assigned into one. (3) Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] says "Invariant: every even-indexed V write zeroes the odd partner" [kv_cache.hpp:2062]; the even set_v path uses _mm512_cvtepu16_epi32 with the comment "cvtepu16_epi32 zeros the odd partner" [kv_cache.hpp:2299-2302]; append_v's comment says even-destination paths zero the odd partner because destinations are fresh ranges [kv_cache.hpp:1868-1871]. (4) The design says "Ordinary row assignment reads and updates a pair, so that pair must already be initialized" [design-text.txt line 430]. So the finding's facts hold and it is not refuted. Two parts of the finding are wrong or overreach. (a) "The partner-preserving rule is new behavior" is only half right: the odd-token set_v path already loads the even half and merges it back [kv_cache.hpp:2305-2320], and the odd-destination append_v paths do the same [kv_cache.hpp:1889-1898, 1908-1918]; only even-token preservation is new. (b) The recommendation to remove the four expression write operations conflicts with Ben's comment #2 (review 5270587330): "Give that type the usual operations that we expect of `tensor` types and, in particular, the row-wise load/store operations" and "convert/slice/compute them freely". The existing tensor's usual operations are construction and assignment from an expr [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:272-282] and view::set(expr) [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:87, 188]. The live issue #4525 scope says "Use the existing expr interface for logical tensor and row operations." These operations are therefore requested interface parity, not speculative additions. Also, the hazard the finding names (a preserving write on a fresh pair leaves indeterminate bytes beside a live token) is not removed by its own recommendation: it keeps view[token][dim] element writes, which also preserve the partner, and set_v(odd) on a never-written pair already does this today (t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2375 and 2462 do it deliberately). The design already separates the two rules ("Keep general expression assignment separate from the conversion rules for adding packed cache rows", line 336; "The cache chooses when to use the behavior for a newly added row", line 334). The row-major V build already writes V through row-view .set(expr) [model.hpp:2821-2823], and the design's v_tensor returns either view type at compile time (line 344), so a packed row type without .set(expr) would break parity between the two V builds. What is genuinely missing is one explicit rule naming which operation cache and model code may use on cache planes, plus the initialization guarantor (the R32 sub-finding).
votes.correction: The four generic write operations (row.set(expr), set_pair, matrix.set(expr), owner expression constructor/assignment) have no production caller in the parent PR, and even-token partner preservation is new (odd-token writes already preserve the even partner today). They should stay, because Ben's comment #2 asks for "the usual operations that we expect of tensor types" and the issue scope says "Use the existing expr interface", and because the row-major V build already writes V through row-view .set(expr) [model.hpp:2821-2823]. Instead of removing them, the design should add one rule: cache and model code (save_v_impl, copy_storage_slot) write cache planes only through append_v_row and the pair operations, never through row.set(expr) or matrix.set(expr); and it should name who guarantees a pair is initialized before row.set(expr) runs. The element write view[token][dim] carries the same partner-preservation property and must be covered by the same rule.

votes.reason:
The finding attacks a choice the design flags as deliberate, and the design already states and tests the hazard the finding raises. The finding's evidence shows only that no production code calls these write paths today. It does not show that adding them is wrong.

1. Ben asked for these operations. His comment #2 (review 5270587330, verbatim in evidence/github-review.json) says: "follow the precedent already present in tron: we currently have types like tensor and dtensor which provide a uniform interface based upon expr" and "Give that type the usual operations that we expect of tensor types and, in particular, the row-wise load/store operations that we need here." In tron the usual operations of a tensor type include construction and assignment from an expr and a view set(expr): tensor.hpp:270-282@f46e48bab498 has `tensor(expr<B,d0,d1,ds...> const& rhs)` and `tensor& operator=(expr<B,d0,d1,ds...> const& rhs)`; view.hpp:87 and view.hpp:188@f46e48bab498 have `view& set(expr<X,...> const& x)` for rank-2 and rank-1 views. The design's row.set(expr), matrix.set(expr) and owner expression constructor/assignment mirror exactly those four members. The live issue body (jhan edited it 2026-09-22) keeps the scope bullet "Use the existing expr interface for logical tensor and row operations."

2. The design flags the choice as deliberate. Section 2, decision for comment #2: "Accept. An at() method for reading one element is not enough. The new type must also support the existing expression interface." Section 2 again: "Add from Ben's earlier request: support the existing expr interface. Allow row expressions, value conversion, and access to selected rows and dimensions with bounds checks."

3. The design already handles the hazard the finding describes (preserving write on fresh storage). Section 6: "Ordinary row assignment must preserve the other row in the pair. ... It cannot use the current behavior of page::set_v(even), which clears the odd row." and "Default storage cannot be read until its values have been written. Ordinary row assignment reads and updates a pair, so that pair must already be initialized." Section 5: "Keep general expression assignment separate from the conversion rules for adding packed cache rows." Section 6: "Keep clearing the odd row when writing an even destination token. Ordinary row assignment must instead preserve the adjacent row." Section 8 has a verification row "Ordinary row assignment" and the row "Zero in the unused partner row" that reruns the scaled_v padding NaN tests through the updated page methods, and the definition of done includes "Tests check the different rules for ordinary row assignment and cache append." A documented precondition is the same guard tron uses today for the zeroing path: kv_cache.hpp:1868-1870@f46e48bab498 "This is safe because append_v is only called via copy_from in append(), where destinations are always fresh ranges."

4. The finding's statement that set_pair has no caller is wrong per the design text. Section 5: "set_pair writes both rows in a pair. ... Provide a form that adds an even token and zeros the odd row in the same pass. It must preserve the current store operation without reading destination bytes." That form is the even-token append primitive used by append_v_row, whose callers are save_v_impl (model.hpp:2818@f46e48bab498) and append_v (kv_cache.hpp:1873/1945). matrix.set(expr) also "Initialize[s] complete pairs", which is set_pair per pair.

5. The hazard argument does not distinguish the removed paths from the path the finding keeps. The recommendation keeps "element writes via view[token][dim] for tests". An element write to an even token does not zero the odd partner either, so "two write rules side by side" remain under the finding's own proposal. Ben's straw-man has the same property: `T& at(size_t token, size_t dim)` returns a writable reference (comment 5765866077).

6. I confirmed the finding's factual base where it matters: at f46e48bab498 the only production writers of packed V are model.hpp:2818 (set_v) and kv_cache.hpp:1945 (append_v inside copy_from), and kv_cache.hpp:2055-2066 states the zeroing invariant. Tests also write packed V by hand: t_amx_numerics.cpp:191-199@f46e48bab498 builds a packed page with a scalar packing loop `v_page[(pair * HEAD_SIZE_128 + d) * 2 + j] = ...`. Once weights_times_v_128x4 takes a vnni_view (design section 5), that test setup needs a typed way to fill a packed owner from row-major data; the owner expression constructor or matrix.set is the natural candidate. So the generic write paths are not without any foreseeable caller, although the design does not name this one.

Residual (note only, no change required to refute): the design could name the intended first callers of the generic write paths (the "Ordinary row assignment" test and the t_amx_numerics setup code that "Update the numerical tests' supporting setup code to match" refers to). The companion point R32 (which load form the preserving path uses on the partner half) is a separate ambiguity and is not part of F09's main claim.

Short version: the code facts in F09 and R32 hold, but the recommendation removes exactly the operations Ben asked for, and the finding does not say so. The surviving part is a small text omission, not a major design change.

What I checked and confirmed:
- set_v (the page method that stores one V row) zero-extends on an even token, so the odd partner becomes 0 [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2296-2303 @f46e48bab498, comment "cvtepu16_epi32 zeros the odd partner"]. The odd path loads the pair as one 64-byte vector [kv_cache.hpp:2312]. append_v even-destination paths zero the partner and the comment says destinations are always fresh ranges [kv_cache.hpp:1868-1871]. Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] states the invariant [kv_cache.hpp:2055-2066].
- Production writers of packed V at f46e48ba are save_v_impl via set_v [h/tron/models/model.hpp:2818] and append_v via copy_from [kv_cache.hpp:1945]. Other set_v callers are tests only (t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:333, t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:98, t/t_llama_unit.cpp several). No production code assigns an expression into packed V. The finding's "exactly two places" claim is correct.
- R32's facts hold: bf16 default constructor leaves content indeterminate [h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp:13-21]; the arena allocator constructs elements only for non-trivially-constructible types [h/system/memory.hpp:333-335]; tests write odd token 7 and odd slot 1 on never-written pairs [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2375, 2462].

Why the finding is refuted under the intent lens:
- Ben's comment #2 (review 5270587330) says verbatim: "we currently have types like `tensor` and `dtensor` which provide a uniform interface based upon `expr`. This allows us to very naturally talk about tensors of various types and convert/slice/compute them freely" and "Give that type the usual operations that we expect of `tensor` types and, in particular, the row-wise load/store operations that we need here."
- The usual operations of tron's tensor types include expression construction and expression assignment. tensor<d0,d1,...> has `tensor(expr<B, d0, d1, ds...> const& rhs)` and `operator=(expr<B, d0, d1, ds...> const&)` [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:269-279 @f46e48bab498]. The rank-2 view has `set(expr<X, d0, d1, ds...> const&)` [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:87] and the rank-1 view has `set(expr<X, d0> const&)` [view.hpp:188].
- F09's recommendation ("Remove row.set(expr), set_pair, matrix.set(expr), and the owner expression constructor/assignment") deletes those operations from the new type. That moves the design away from Ben's #2 and from the issue #4525 scope bullet "Use the existing expr interface for logical tensor and row operations" (issue body, facts.md). The finding does not mention either.
- jhan's prompt asked codex to "Synthesize claude design and Ben's comments #2 and #3" (codex-add-tensor-type.md, step 2). The design's section 2 does this explicitly: "Add from Ben's earlier request: support the existing expr interface." Removing the expr writes would undo that synthesis.

Why the remaining risk is already handled or small:
- The design states the precondition for ordinary row assignment: "Ordinary row assignment reads and updates a pair, so that pair must already be initialized" and "Full-matrix assignment must initialize complete pairs without reading destination bytes" (design section 6). It keeps append_v_row as the only cache append path with the zeroing rule (section 5, "Separate adding cache rows from ordinary assignment"). It forbids scalar loops for the V operations (step 2: "Do not replace these vector operations with scalar loops") and reads chunks with vector operations (section 5 table, "matrix[token].chunk(i)"). So the implementer would not build the wrong thing, and R32's undefined-behavior concern is covered by the stated precondition plus the vector-read rule.
- The "later caller misuses the preserving path" argument is a hazard of any tensor type with element writes, including the `view[token][dim]` writes that F09 itself wants to keep. It is a judgment call, not a defect that blocks Ben's acceptance.
votes.correction: Omission (minor): the design provides expression writes into packed V (row.set(expr), matrix.set(expr), owner expression constructor and assignment) as Ben's comment #2 asks ("the usual operations that we expect of tensor types"), but it does not say that no production caller in the parent PR uses them, and it names no party that guarantees the pair is initialized before row.set. Add three sentences: (1) "In the parent PR the only production writers of packed V are save_v_impl [model.hpp:2818] and append_v [kv_cache.hpp:1945]; both go through append_v_row. The expression write operations have no production caller in the parent and are exercised by the tests in section 8." (2) "The caller guarantees that a pair is initialized before ordinary row assignment. Appending an even token or a full-matrix assignment initializes it." (3) "row.set on packed V reads the partner through one 64-byte vector pair load, as set_v does today [kv_cache.hpp:2312], never through scalar bf16 element reads." Also reword Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] from "every even-indexed V write zeroes the odd partner" to "every cache append of an even token zeroes the odd partner", so the Note stays true once ordinary assignment exists. Keep the operations; do not remove them.

rejected.title: Rvalue deletion needs const&& and all-or-none ref-qualification
rejected.claim: Omission: deleting an rvalue-qualified overload is legal and useful (a temporary owner's as_view() or operator[] fails at compile time), but C++ forbids mixing ref-qualified and unqualified overloads of the same name, so as_view() needs the full set: &, const&, && = delete, const&& = delete. Ben's straw-man and the design list only &, const& and && = delete; a const rvalue (for example a function returning const vnni_tensor by value) then binds to the const& overload and yields a view of a dead temporary. Ref-qualifiers are not special member functions, so they do not affect trivial copyability, and tensor's std::construct_at(&data[i], rhs[i]) constructs tensor<d1> rows, not the owner, so there is no interaction there.

rejected.design_quote: Delete overloads for rvalue owners (temporary values or objects marked for moving). [...] Apply the same restriction to owner indexing. Apply it to every function returning access to the owner's storage without a copy.
rejected.recommendation: Spell out the four overloads for as_view() and for operator[]: `&`, `const&`, `&& = delete`, `const&& = delete`, and note that all overloads of each name must carry a ref-qualifier.

- The same design table row already says: "PR #4424 only. Keep the existing layout-selection condition. Keep the kernel restricted to 64 tokens × 128 dimensions." Section 1 states "A page holds 64 token positions." So R = 64 and the no-generalization rule are both already stated where the formula appears.

Writing K's formula with a literal 4 would make it the only row that hardcodes a shape-derived constant, inconsistent with the design's own convention and with the child's `PAGE_TOKENS_64 / BLOCK_TOKENS_16`.

Net: the finding contains no factual error about the design, and the ambiguity it asserts is already closed by the design's restriction in the same row. No change to the design is required.

(design-text.txt:186), so the parent implementer never implements it and the restriction is stated where the formula is; (2) R is the compile-time Rows argument of the design's proposed types, "template <typename T, size_t Rows, size_t Cols> class vnni_view" (design-text.txt:223-224), the same way D is used in the V formula of the same table, not a runtime knob; (3) section 5 excludes "Shapes chosen at runtime" and "A general system for selecting layouts through a policy type" (design-text.txt:300, 304); (4) the child step says "Move K scatter and gather ... into the typed representation. Move the block write there too" and "Select the K owner and view using the existing conditions on storage geometry" (design-text.txt:490, 492), i.e. move existing code under the existing head_size == 128 gate; (5) the child's own cache layer already expresses the block count as R/16: "TRON_ASSERT_LT(c, page_size / k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16);" (child h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1728), where page_size is the kv_block<page_size, head_size> template parameter (main f46e48ba kv_cache.hpp:2190, value 64 at :1455), so R/16 mirrors the child's own notation rather than introducing a foreign parameter. The finding acknowledges the design's restriction, attacks a notation choice the design pairs with an explicit restriction, and offers no evidence that an implementer would misread it ("suggests ... could try"). Under the fairness lens this is refuted. Naming TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 in the design would be an optional cross-reference, not a needed change.

The finding's facts about the child hold, but its recommendation contradicts Ben's stated intent, and its reading of the design's "64x128 restriction" is wrong.

Facts I confirmed in the child (k_vnni.hpp @30c4ac82cbb6): TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = PAGE_TOKENS_64 / BLOCK_TOKENS_16 at line 52; the static_assert pinning TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 == 4 is at lines 76-80 (the finding says ~78-82); index() uses TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 at lines 101-107; both pair_base overloads at 113-123; scatter_row at 139-146. So the child has no R parameter. That part is correct.

Why the finding is refuted on intent:
1. The design's formula is Ben's formula, variable-for-variable. Ben's comment #3 straw-man (github-review.json, comments[3]) defines `template <size_t Tokens, size_t Dims> struct k_vnni_layout` with `static_assert(Tokens > 0 && Tokens % 16 == 0)` and `offset()` returning `((((step * (Tokens / 16) + block) * 16 + pair) * 16 + lane) * 2) + dim % 2`. The design's row writes `((((dimension / 32) * (R / 16) + token / 16) * 16 + (dimension % 32) / 2) * 16 + token % 16) * 2 + dimension % 2` with "R is the stored token count." That is `Tokens / 16` renamed. Recommending "write 4" and "do not generalize it" would move the design away from Ben's sketch without saying so.
2. Ben explicitly wants the layout type more general than the kernel: "These restrictions describe storage. Kernels can impose stricter restrictions. For example, representing k_vnni_layout<128, 256> would not imply that the current AMX kernel supports it." The design mirrors this: the same row says "Keep the kernel restricted to 64 tokens x 128 dimensions" (a restriction on the kernel, not on the type), and two paragraphs later "A tensor type can represent a shape that an attention kernel does not support." The finding's phrase "against the design's own 64x128 restriction" misreads a kernel restriction as a type restriction.
3. A Rows parameter is unavoidable, so R/16 is the natural form. The storage owner the type must live in is `template <size_t page_size, size_t head_size> struct kv_block` (kv_cache.hpp:2190-2191 @f46e48bab498), and the design's interface is `vnni_tensor<Rows, Cols>` / `vnni_view<T, Rows, Cols>` (design section 5). A blocked-K view inside a Rows-templated class that hardcodes 4 would need an extra static_assert(Rows == 64) and would diverge from Ben's `Tokens / 16` for no gain. Threading Rows/16 through the address helpers is what typing the layout means; it is not a risk to warn against.
4. The child's hardcoded constants are exactly the code Ben asked to replace (comment #2: "too many bf16_t* pointers with no layout hint"; #3: typed layout/storage/view). They are not the reference the parent design should conform to.
5. The design correctly marks the row "PR #4424 only", so nothing in the parent PR is affected either way.

Consequence for the implementing agent: none. The formula as written is correct for R = 64 (the finding's own enumeration confirms this) and matches both Ben's sketch and the design's Rows-templated interface. No text change is needed.
votes.correction: The design's R/16 form is Ben's `Tokens / 16` from his comment #3 straw-man, renamed; it should stay. The child (k_vnni.hpp @30c4ac82cbb6:52, 76-80, 101-123) hardcodes TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = 4 because it has no typed layout, which is what Ben asked to change. Optionally the design could add one clause: "R is the kv_block page_size template argument (64 for every current page); this matches Ben's Tokens / 16." Not required.

votes.reason:
The finding's description of the script holds. check_layouts.py (issue4525/evidence/check_layouts.py) builds physical_order for V at lines 9-10 as nested loops "for p in range(0, rows, 2) for d in range(cols) for lane in range(2)" (pair, dim, lane) and for K at lines 19-21 as "for step in range(4) for block in range(4) for pair in range(16) for token in range(16) for lane in range(2)" (step, block, pair, token, lane). Both nestings are the loop form of the closed formulas asserted at lines 12 and 23-24. The file contains no reference to the kv_block declaration, to set_v, or to k_vnni.hpp; the order is the script author's transcription. So the check proves "closed form == nested-loop restatement", not "closed form == C++ storage order".

The design sentence quoted is verbatim at design-text.txt:206 / HTML line 142: "The script lists values in storage order and checks every calculated position against that list. All positions match." The design does add "It does not test a C++ implementation", which the finding accounts for by grading this a note.

I re-derived the layouts from primary sources and they agree with the design formulas, as the finding states. Sources: kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2196-2198 declares "bf16s v[page_size / 2][head_size / chunk_size * 2]" with comment "[p/2][i/C][i%C][p%2]"; simd/auto.hpp@f46e48bab498:54 "using bf16s = bf16x16" so one pair row is 2*D elements; set_v (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2289-2320) sets v_ptr = &v[i_page/2], stores at v_ptr + i*2, even token via _mm512_cvtepu16_epi32 (value in low half of each dword = even element offset), odd token via slli 16 (high half = odd offset). Simulating those lanes in Python (no file written) reproduces (token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2 for D in {64,128,256,512}, 64 tokens each. For K, k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:113-142: pair_base dword index = (s*4 + c)*256 + t, scatter offsets dp*16 dwords, dword dp = row[s*32+2dp], row[s*32+2dp+1]; simulating the scatter reproduces (((s*4+c)*16+dp)*16+t)*2+j for all 8192 elements, and the seven anchors (0,0)->0, (0,1)->1, (1,0)->2, (0,2)->32, (16,0)->512, (0,32)->2048, (63,127)->8191 hold.

One small mislabel in the finding's evidence field: it calls the anchors "Design table anchors". The anchor coordinates appear only in check_layouts.py:28-29; the design page has no occurrence of 8191, 2048 or the coordinate pairs (grep count 0), its table says only "7 selected coordinates with known positions". This does not affect the claim.
votes.correction: The anchor coordinates cited as "Design table anchors" live in check_layouts.py lines 28-29, not in a design table; the design table only says "7 selected coordinates with known positions". Otherwise the claim stands: the script's "storage order" list is the nested-loop restatement of the closed formulas, chosen by the script author, and the design's source basis for the order is the S1 (kv_cache.hpp) and S10 (k_vnni.hpp) links, not the script.

votes.reason:
Two grounds, both checked against the sources.

1. The design already scopes the check the way the finding wants. The quoted sentence is followed directly by: "This checks the formulas in the design. It does not test a C++ implementation." [design-text.txt line 206; design-new-tensor-type.html line 142]. The results file the sentence links to labels itself "kind": "design arithmetic check, not a C++ implementation test" [issue4525/evidence/layout-checks.json line 2]. The formula table cites the source files [S1] [S10] as the provenance of the layouts [design-text.txt line 188]. So the page tells the reader: layouts come from the source, the script checks only the arithmetic of the closed forms, and nothing in C++ was tested. That is exactly what the script does.

2. The finding's factual premise is not supported. It states the loops "transcribe the formula's structure" and do "not derive order from the kv_block declaration". The kv_block comment at main documents V's index nesting as "[p/2][i/C][i%C][p%2]" (pair, chunk, dim-in-chunk, parity) [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498 lines 2193-2196]. The script's V loop order is pair, dim, lane (parity) [check_layouts.py lines 9-10]. Those are the same nesting, so the loops transcribe the declaration's documented order just as much as the formula. For K, the child header says index() is "the formula of the header comment" [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6 lines 99-107], and pair_base plus scatter_row realize the same dword addresses: byte = ((s*4+c)*256 + t)*4 plus dp*64 [lines 113-118, 127-139]. The script's K loop order (step, block, pair, token, lane) is that nesting [check_layouts.py lines 19-21]. set_v's even path stores the even token in the low half of each dword at v_ptr + i*2 (cvtepu16_epi32), which is lane 0 of the pair [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498 lines 2299-2303]; that matches lane order in the enumeration. The finding's own independent derivation agrees at all sizes. So the "storage order" list IS the source-documented storage order, and the design sentence "The script lists values in storage order" is literally true. The check also has real content within its stated scope: the enumerate-index equality plus len(set(...)) == rows*cols [lines 12-13, 26-27] proves the closed form is a bijection with the correct multipliers, and a typo such as (token/2)*D would fail it.

The finding's proposed replacement wording ("Order was not derived from the C++ declaration or the store instructions") would assert a provenance the evidence contradicts, since the loop nesting equals the declaration comment's nesting. The finding concedes the formulas stand and rates itself a note. An optional harmless addition would be one clause naming where the enumeration order comes from ("the loop order follows the index nesting documented in the kv_block comment and the k_vnni header comment"), but no change is required.

Short version: the design sentence is literally true, the design already discloses the limit the finding asks it to disclose, and the change has no consequence for the implementing agent or for Ben. So this is a wording preference, not a defect.

Evidence checked:

1. The list is in storage order. I simulated set_v's store lanes (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2296-2319: v_ptr = &v[i_page/2]; even token = cvtepu16_epi32 -> low half of dword k; odd token = slli 16 -> high half; pair row = 2*D bf16 because bf16s = bf16x16 at simd/auto.hpp@f46e48bab498:54 and kv_block_at_storage asserts sizeof(kv_block) == 2*page_size*head_size*sizeof(bf16)). Every (token, dim) position equals the design's V formula at D = 64, 128, 256, 512. I simulated pair_base + scatter_row dword addresses (k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:118-147: byte offset ((s*4+c)*256 + t)*4, row dp adds dp*16 dwords, low half = even dim). Every position equals the design's K formula and the 7 anchors. So "The script lists values in storage order" (design-text.txt line 206, HTML line 142) is a true statement, not an overstatement.

2. The finding's attribution is unsupported. It says the loops "transcribe the formula's structure" and do "not derive order from the kv_block declaration". But the script's V nesting (pair, dim, lane) is exactly the declaration's documented index order "[p/2][i/C][i%C][p%2]" (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2197-2198), and its K nesting (step, block, pair, token, lane) is exactly the header comment's order "(s, c, dp, t, j)" (k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:23-27). From the script alone one cannot say whether the order was taken from the formula or from the source comments; they are the same order.

3. The design already states the limit. The same paragraph says "This checks the formulas in the design. It does not test a C++ implementation." (design-text.txt line 206), and the results file labels itself "design arithmetic check, not a C++ implementation test" (evidence/layout-checks.json). The finding's proposed sentence adds only a provenance clause to a caveat that is already present.

4. No consequence under the INTENT lens. Neither Ben's comments #2/#3 nor jhan's prompt (codex-add-tensor-type.md) ask for a layout-check script. The implementing agent must build from kv_block and set_v regardless, and the design's verification table already requires byte-size, plane-offset and alignment checks against the C++ block (design-text.txt line 524). Ben will review C++ code, not this Python script. The finding itself concedes "the formulas stand" and rates itself "note", yet recommends a text change; the change would not alter what anyone builds or accepts.

Residual truth in the finding: the script does not simulate store instructions, so it cannot catch a misread of the C++ layout. That is a fair remark about verification strength, but the design does not claim instruction-level verification, so nothing needs to change.
votes.correction: check_layouts.py is a self-consistency check: its enumeration order equals the documented index order in the kv_block comment (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2197-2198) and the k_vnni.hpp header (30c4ac82cbb6:23-27), and it does not simulate set_v lanes or scatter_row addresses. An independent simulation of those instructions matches the design's V formula at D = 64/128/256/512 and the K formula at 64x128. The design already says the script checks the formulas and not a C++ implementation, so the sentence "The script lists values in storage order ..." is accurate and needs no change. Adding an instruction-level simulation is optional.

lens_verdicts.issue-capture: Partly. The live issue #4525 captures jhan's action item 4 (a standalone PR that types the existing packed V and native K caches on main, with #4424 rebased onto it afterwards), keeps Ben's comment #1 (save_k worker index) separate as jhan asked, is assigned to jhan-positron as requested, and its three links (review 5270587330, comment 5765866077, discussion r4065141577) match the saved JSON and the live GitHub API. The gaps: the body has no problem statement and does not define "packed V", "native K" or "packed-K", so it is not self-contained for a reader who has not seen the PR thread; three explicit constraints from Ben's straw-man (construct typed storage in the arena instead of casting, no way to relabel a raw pointer as a packed view, no implicit clearing on hot allocation paths) are not stated; the body names "Ben" twice against jhan's no-names rule; and after jhan's rename the design page still says "before PR #4424" in its title, Short version and section 3 while its saved evidence files hold the old issue text. Section 2's comment table is correct on sources, times and edit time against the JSON, but it omits the date and the GitHub ids.
lens_verdicts.ben-fidelity: jhan's reading is right: Ben's doubt concerns only the separate layout type, so the address mapping belongs in the view, and storage stays a separate owner (Ben's sketch is not a chain "layout -> storage -> view"; the Layout is a template parameter of both storage and view). Codex's synthesis keeps every hard requirement of Ben's straw-man (private pointer constructor, no data(), mutable-to-const only, friend detail::vnni_access, in-block aligned storage, typed kernel parameters, arena constructs the type, zero-init invariant, optimized bulk paths) and of review #2 (expr precedent, row-wise load/store). It is not faithful on process and on three points: it treats Ben's open doubt as a decision without naming the two-type-family consequence, it overrides Ben's const rule while citing a repository precedent that is mixed (the rank-1 view states Ben's rule verbatim), and it drops at() and adds operator[], slices and iterators without flagging them as deviations. "No clarification from Ben is needed" is not defensible under jhan's item 3 ("if you disagree ... stop here"); the design should carry a short list of questions for Ben before implementation.
lens_verdicts.cpp-interface: The section 5 interface is expressible with tron's existing expr machinery. A vnni_view that inherits expr<view,R,D> and whose operator[] returns a vnni_row inheriting expr<row,D> with chunk() and bf16_chunk() satisfies tensor<d0,d1>(expr const&) and operator= (tensor.hpp:270-282 via tensor<d1>(expr<B,d1> const&) at 79-85) and dtensor's pad()/block() path (hardware/tensor.hpp:128-162, 385-395); the rank-2 view failing the `expression` concept matches the existing rank-2 view and blocks nothing the design needs; the trivially-default-constructible owner with a defaulted default constructor plus a converting expr constructor is consistent because bf16() = default is trivial (bf16.hpp:22, 81) and template constructors are never special members. Two guidance gaps must be closed before implementation: the "placement construction" wording must exclude std::construct_at and value-initialization, which zero the arena, and the design must state whether the packed types compile in the 8-lane build, where the unconditional fake kernel definitions will instantiate them. The remaining findings are admissions, naming, and mechanics the implementing agent would otherwise guess.
lens_verdicts.behavior-preservation: (1) Not unambiguous: the design never states which operation save_v_impl calls, and two of its sentences point the model path at pair-preserving ordinary assignment, which would leave stale odd rows on reused offsets and break the zero-padding invariant that scaled_v relies on (blocker). (2), (3), (5), (7) each need one added paragraph (minor findings); the design's conversion description for the set_v path is confirmed correct against kv_cache.hpp:2342/2382, and the only divergence from fp32s_to_bf16s is for NaN-exponent inputs with nonzero low 16 bits. (4) No production overlapping copy exists: copy_from is called only from book::append, which copies between two different books (full.hpp:1333 asserts my_book != parent_book; 1342), so "other overlapping copies need not work" is safe. (6) GOF staging is consistent with full.hpp:2644-2657 (k_head_fn returns the K row's .data; v_head_fn unpacks via get_v into the caller's scratch). (8) The kv_block constraints hold: storage_alignment = kv_block_alignment = 64 bytes in both builds, and a single alignas(64) array owner keeps sizeof and alignof unchanged.
lens_verdicts.pr-split-process: The design's revision table inverts the two main commits: 98bb8cb2 is the live main tip (git ls-remote, 2026-09-22) and f46e48ba is only PR 4424's recorded base, so the implementing agent must branch from origin/main at or after 98bb8cb2 and re-pin the shifted line references (production caller sets are unchanged; one new test caller of page::set_v exists). The section 3 diagram and steps deliver jhan's "new PR, then #4424 atop it" split, #4424 is draft as required, and the AGENTS.md quotes are accurate paraphrases, but the child step omits changing #4424's GitHub base to the parent branch, the main-side rebase conflicts, and a method for replaying 22 commits. No required CI job can build with TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON today (the flag exists only in the manual legacy workflow, and PR 4505 adds it to the nightly deb preset only), so S13's demand is a CI-policy decision for jhan rather than an instruction the agent may execute, and the parent's new behavior tests must live in t_llama_unit to satisfy the AGENTS.md test rule.
lens_verdicts.simplicity-scope: No production caller at main f46e48bab498 or at the main tip 98bb8cb22f94 slices a packed V plane, iterates one, or assigns an expression into one: V is touched only by save_v_impl (page::set_v, one token from a raw row pointer), the AMX PV kernel (page::v_data, whole plane), page::scaled_v (whole plane), GOF staging (page::get_v into caller scratch) and append_v inside copy_storage_slot (one token, packed to packed). The minimal parent is therefore: a V owner and typed view with element access and a read-only row expression, bulk store_row for bf16/fp16/float with today's set_v bodies, bulk load_row with today's get_v body, a packed-to-packed token copy with append_v's four branches, typed parameters for weights_times_v_128x4 and qk_rowmajor_128x4 plus their test fakes, and removal of page::v_data and kv_block::v_base. Slices, iteration, matrix.set(expr), the owner-from-expression constructor, set_pair and the partner-preserving row.set(expr) have no caller and should be deferred. Native K needs no new type: page::k already returns view<bf16,true,false,seq<64,128>> and save_k_impl already writes K through a typed row .set(expr), so the parent is "type packed V + type the two AMX kernel parameters".
lens_verdicts.handoff-actionability: Not yet actionable without guessing. The design is right about the layout facts and its 38 source links hold up (15 spot-checked, all support their sentences), but an implementing agent would have to guess in five places: which existing page functions (k, set_v, get_v, v, v_ptr, append_v, v_base) are kept, renamed or removed and what the model and the FPGA staging code call instead; how to run the two "generated code" completion checks; which host and flags to build on (sw-dev-01 is not a repository or user rule, and this box has no nix); what to do about the required-CI gap the design itself reports; and the revision table labels the live main tip 98bb8cb2 as stale. Fix those and the design can be handed over.
lens_verdicts.formulas-and-page: Lens A: the design's packed-V formula and all four plane sizes are correct, derived independently from the kv_block declaration and from set_v's store lanes (64x64=8192 B, 64x128=16384 B, 64x256=32768 B, 64x512=65536 B). The blocked-K formula matches the child's pair_base plus scatter_row byte addressing for R=64, and the child hardcodes 4 token blocks, so "R/16" is a generalization the code does not have. "Not a transpose of V" is true for the whole plane (7680 of 8192 positions differ) but each 16-token x 32-dimension tile is exactly the transposed packed-V formula. check_layouts.py is not a strict tautology but it enumerates order from loops that mirror the formula's nesting, not from the declaration or the store code; head_size 64 is legal on all three paths (kv_block %16, set_v %32, scaled_v in {64,128,256,512}), and the design's 16-divisibility rule matches kv_block, not set_v, while saying only that stricter store rules stay in force.

critic_overall: Accept with changes. The design reads Ben's two typed-access comments correctly, keeps the right invariants in view (zero odd partner, truncating fp16/float conversion, trivial construction with no arena clearing, byte-identical kv_block size), and gives a workable parent-then-child order, so the direction does not need a redo. It cannot go to an implementing agent as written: the panel's F01 (which V write operation the model calls) would let the padding invariant regress silently, and the majors on accessor mapping, 8-lane compile rules, construction form and CI evidence must be answered first. The items I add are narrower: the EAGLE storage wording names two different buffers, two scheduler rules that depend on the pair layout are unlisted (one added on main after the snapshot), one test file with a 256-dimension float V write is missing from the step list, the child section lacks an accessor mapping and a K write-granularity rule that the shared block save depends on, and the prose Notes have no step. None of these blocks the parent PR, and all can be fixed with a few sentences each. After F02's questions to Ben are answered and the confirmed majors are folded in, the page is a sound handoff.
